agent_notes: The heading is a rubric, not a verse of speech. 'To the choirmaster' follows the usual reading of lamnatseach (Piel participle of natsach); the exact sense of the root in the headings is uncertain, so the commentary says so. 'To make remembrance' (lehazkir) is rendered literally; Rashi reads it as a prayer that God remember the speaker, Metzudat David as a prayer that God hasten to save, and I keep the ambiguity.

agent_notes: The verse has no verb of its own in the first line: 'God, to deliver me' is an ellipsis, and the single imperative chushah at the end serves both lines (Radak, Meiri, Metzudat David). The literal layer keeps the broken syntax; the dramatic layer supplies the haste. KJV and ASV supply 'Make haste' at the front and again in the second line, and YLT keeps the ellipsis, which I follow.

STEPBible glosses yachperu as 'abashed'; I kept it close to that. The root chpr here is 'be ashamed, blush', not 'dig'. 'Seek my nefesh' is kept literal ('life'), since the sense is hostile pursuit to kill (Malbim reads it as seeking to kill me). ASV 'delight in my hurt' reads chafetsei as 'take pleasure in'; the Hebrew participle is 'desiring', which can be either, and I kept the plain 'desiring'.

agent_notes: 'ekev has two senses in the commentators: 'heel, rear' (Ibn Ezra's first reading, Rashi 'in the very same track') and 'consequence, reward' (Radak, Metzudat Zion, Meiri). I kept 'on the heel of their shame' in the literal layer, and let the commentary give both. KJV 'for a reward' takes the second sense.
